title: Lotus Recognition 002 — when finding the shortcut costs more
question: Can a learner infer the elementary row-edit relationship to a stored Boolean matrix—and does that recognition repay its own work, compared to fresh solving and exact caching?
method: Pinned baseline inverse-update algorithm, four compared policies, exact candidate row comparison, paid recognition/repair/checking/storage ledgers, finite workload sweeps, and separate certificate audits.
finding: In a specified 16-dimensional immediate related chain, paid transfer costs 2,159,593 units versus 2,906,281 fresh and 2,545,438 exact; on a strict 64-parent search, search alone costs 23,126 versus 6,643 for an entire fresh checked query. Recorded audit checks 904,176 raw certificates across the four policies.
claim_scope: Finite generated affine matrix workloads and declared equal-weight event-accounting model; not a general P-vs-NP claim, wall-clock speedup proof, or autonomous discovery of a new operation.
limitations: The repair identity was previously known; the learner recognizes only a supported one-row edit.
The 594 grid scenarios include repeated arrivals and generator-designed relationships, not random real-world workloads.
A growing archive may cost more to scan than simply solving; false near-matches exacerbate the loss.
The compressed 41 MB archive includes historical code and large run data; public candidate is deliberately selective.
open_questions: Can a charged structural index reduce search without hiding its construction or maintenance costs?
Does the improvement survive held-out relations, stronger solvers, and machine-level performance accounting?

provenance.origin: This project-specific recognition experiment builds on preserved earlier owner-directed baseline; the new learner experiment is separate from that historical baseline.
provenance.change_note: First curated Proof Wall candidate. No modification to original scientific evidence or source archive. Preparation v2: removed private source links and identifiers from the public-facing report and article; disclosed incomplete executable dependencies and the operation-cost model. Full originals preserved privately. The derivative protocol also replaces private baseline identifiers with a private-custody reference. Derivative report and protocol are labeled in-file. Release v3 records owner approval of the prepared v2 selection ; article and underlying evidence files remain unchanged. The article retains its earlier preparation-stage wording; the owner subsequently approved this release and publication review has been completed.
